context.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
context.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊆V_K, if x_K(W)⊆W, y_K(W)⊆W and h_K(W)⊆W, then W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L_K-module, for every field K of characteristic p and every integer 0≤λ<p, including λ=0 and p=2.

record.statement: Let A be any semiring satisfying the strong rank condition (every injective A-linear map A^s→A^t between finite free modules forces s≤t). Let T be a finite indexing type, and let F_t, t∈T, be additive commutative monoids with A-module structures, each free and finitely generated over A. Then Module.finrank_A(∏_{t∈T}F_t)=Σ_{t∈T}Module.finrank_A(F_t), where finrank is the natural-number value of module rank (and agrees with finite vector-space dimension over a field).

record.statement: n=λ+1>0, I has n elements, and (e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V. For all integers d≥0, hy^d v=(λ-2d)y^d v, and for d≥1, xy^d v=d(λ-d+1)y^(d-1)v. For all d>λ, y^d v=0. For i∈I: xe_0=0; xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_(i-1) if i≥1; ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) if i<λ and ye_λ=0; he_i=(λ-2i)e_i. For every integer r≥0 and i∈I, X_r e_i=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_(i-r) if r≤i and is zero if r>i; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ and is zero otherwise.

record.statement: μ is injective. Identifying M_R with μ(M_R)⊆V, M_R is free of rank n over R, its complex span is V, and every X_r,Y_r (r≥0) preserves it. For all i,j∈I the integer binom(λ,j) is a unit of R and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1) X_(λ-i) Y_λ X_λ Y_(λ-j). In particular every E_ij preserves M_R.

record.statement: n>0, (e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V, μ is injective, and the identified M_R⊆V is free of rank n over R and spans V over C. For every i∈I, J_i=J. The R-submodule J⊆C is finitely generated and nonzero, and M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i inside V; explicitly the map (c_i)_{i∈I}↦Σ_{i∈I}c_i e_i is an R-linear isomorphism from the finite product J^I to M_R.

record.statement: n>0 and there exists a K-basis B=(B_i)_{i∈I} of V_K. On this basis x_K B_0=0, x_K B_i=(λ-i+1)B_(i-1) for 1≤i≤λ; y_K B_i=(i+1)B_(i+1) for 0≤i<λ and y_K B_λ=0; h_K B_i=(λ-2i)B_i. These are exactly the induced actions of x,y,h, so they define the stated L_K-action. All integer coefficients here are mapped into K. For 0≤r≤λ, r! is nonzero in K; define A_r=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r and C_r=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r. For i,j∈I let T_ij be the K-linear map B_j↦B_i with all other basis vectors mapped to zero. Then binom(λ,j) is nonzero in K and T_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1) A_(λ-i) C_λ A_λ C_(λ-j). Moreover A_r,C_r are precisely the induced divided powers X_r,Y_r on V_K.
